risk.description: Failure mode detection and risk assessment

methods.name: Stakeholder Round Table
methods.description: Every user type and stakeholder gets a seat at the table. Each voices their needs independently before any synthesis. Use when requirements feel one-sided or missing perspectives.

methods.name: Expert Panel Review
methods.description: Domain experts review the spec from their specialty lens. Each expert identifies gaps, risks, and domain-specific requirements that generalists miss. Use for regulated or specialized domains.

methods.name: Debate Club Showdown
methods.description: Two opposing positions debate a design decision. The affirmative must defend with evidence; the negative must attack with evidence. Observer judges the strongest argument. Use for controversial architecture choices.

methods.name: User Persona Focus Group
methods.description: Each persona is embodied by an agent that experiences the proposed flow end-to-end. Agents report friction points, delight moments, and gaps specific to their persona's context. Use when UX needs validation across diverse users.

methods.name: Time Traveler Council
methods.description: Past you (Day 1), present you (Day N), and future you (2 years later) review the design. Past-you questions complexity. Future-you warns about maintenance. Use when design has long-term implications.

methods.name: Cross-Functional War Room
methods.description: Dev, QA, Ops, Security, and Product simultaneously stress-test the spec from their functional perspective. Each role identifies what will break in their domain. Use before implementation commitment.

methods.name: Mentor and Apprentice
methods.description: A senior expert explains the design to a junior who questions everything. The junior's naive questions expose unstated assumptions. The mentor's explanations reveal implicit knowledge. Use when design feels 'obvious' to experts.

methods.name: Good Cop Bad Cop
methods.description: One agent is aggressively critical of every design choice. Another is supportively constructive. The tension reveals which concerns are legitimate and which are noise. Use when consensus forms too quickly.

methods.name: Improv Yes-And
methods.description: Each agent builds on the previous agent's idea. No criticism allowed. Ideas compound multiplicatively. Use when stuck in local optima or when existing solutions feel inadequate.

methods.name: Customer Support Theater
methods.description: Simulate users calling support about the proposed design. What do they get confused by? What errors do they hit? What workarounds do they invent? Use when UX needs real-world stress testing.

methods.name: Tree of Thoughts
methods.description: Explore multiple reasoning paths simultaneously. Each branch explores a different approach. Branches compete and cross-pollinate. Use for complex decisions with many viable options.

methods.name: Graph of Thoughts
methods.description: Ideas form a graph with edges representing relationships. The graph reveals clusters, bridges, and orphans. Use when the problem space is interconnected and non-linear.

methods.name: Thread of Thought
methods.description: Follow a single reasoning thread deeply without branching. Push through intermediate confusions. Use when surface-level analysis keeps hitting the same depth limit.

methods.name: Self-Consistency Validation
methods.description: Generate multiple independent analyses of the same problem. Compare for consistency. Divergent conclusions indicate underspecification or hidden complexity. Use to detect specification ambiguity.

methods.name: Meta-Prompting Analysis
methods.description: Examine the thinking process itself. What assumptions did the analysis make? What methods were used? Are there better methods? Use when results feel suspiciously clean or convenient.

methods.name: Reasoning via Planning
methods.description: Plan the implementation step by step. Each step reveals requirements, dependencies, and constraints that abstract analysis misses. Use when the gap between spec and implementation feels large.

methods.name: Red Team vs Blue Team
methods.description: Red Team attacks the design from every angle (security, reliability, UX, cost). Blue Team defends and patches. Use for security-critical or high-stakes systems.

methods.name: Shark Tank Pitch
methods.description: Pitch the design to skeptical investors. They challenge business model, market fit, technical feasibility. Must defend with data. Use when building a product for real users/markets.

methods.name: Code Review Gauntlet
methods.description: The spec goes through a gauntlet of reviewers: security, performance, accessibility, maintainability, testability. Each reviewer must find at least 3 issues. Use before Phase 4 implementation.

methods.name: Architecture Decision Records
methods.description: Every significant architectural choice is documented as an ADR with context, decision, alternatives considered, and consequences. Makes trade-offs explicit and reversible. Use for all architecture decisions.

methods.name: Rubber Duck Debugging Evolved
methods.description: Explain the entire design to a rubber duck that asks clarifying questions. The act of explanation reveals gaps. The questions reveal assumptions. Use when design feels complete but untested.

methods.name: Algorithm Olympics
methods.description: Multiple algorithmic approaches compete on the same problem. Each is benchmarked on correctness, performance, readability, and maintainability. Use for performance-critical paths.

methods.name: Security Audit Personas
methods.description: Different attacker personas (script kiddie, insider threat, nation-state, opportunistic) audit the design. Each has different capabilities and motivations. Use for comprehensive threat modeling.

methods.name: Performance Profiler Panel
methods.description: Latency, throughput, memory, and cost profilers analyze the design. Each identifies bottlenecks and scaling limits. Use before committing to an architecture.

methods.name: SCAMPER Method
methods.description: Substitute, Combine, Adapt, Modify, Put to another use, Eliminate, Reverse. Apply each operation to the design. Use when stuck or when the solution feels derivative.
methods.output: substitute-ideas → combine-ideas → adapt-ideas → modify-ideas → eliminate-ideas → reverse-ideas

methods.name: Reverse Engineering
methods.description: Start from the desired end state and work backwards. What must exist just before the end? One step before that? Reveals the minimum viable path. Use for goal-driven design.

methods.name: What If Scenarios
methods.description: What if users are offline? What if data is 100x larger? What if the API is down for an hour? What if a competitor launches tomorrow? Stress-test through extreme scenarios.

methods.name: Random Input Stimulus
methods.description: Introduce a random concept from an unrelated domain. Force connections to the design problem. Use when all ideas feel too similar or conventional.

methods.name: Exquisite Corpse Brainstorm
methods.description: Each agent adds to the design without seeing the full previous contribution. The partial reveals produce unexpected combinations. Use for breaking out of local optima.

methods.name: Genre Mashup
methods.description: Apply design patterns from a completely different industry. What would a game designer do? A filmmaker? A chef? Use when the solution space feels narrow.

methods.name: Literature Review Personas
methods.description: Agents embody different research traditions (academic, industry, open-source, competitor). Each surveys their domain for relevant prior art. Use when building in a mature domain.

methods.name: Thesis Defense Simulation
methods.description: The design must defend itself against a committee of skeptical examiners. Each examiner specializes in a different critique angle. Use to harden the design before implementation.

methods.name: Comparative Analysis Matrix
methods.description: Map the proposed design against alternatives across multiple weighted dimensions. Quantify trade-offs. Use when choosing between competing approaches.

methods.name: Pre-mortem Analysis
methods.description: Assume the project failed. Work backwards to identify everything that could have caused the failure. Use before committing significant resources.

methods.name: Failure Mode Analysis
methods.description: For each component, identify: how it can fail, probability, impact, detection method, mitigation. Systematic FMEA approach. Use for reliability-critical systems.

methods.name: Challenge from Critical Perspective
methods.description: Appoint a devil's advocate to challenge every assumption. Nothing is sacred. Every design choice must survive skeptical scrutiny. Use when team confidence is high but unexamined.

methods.name: Identify Potential Risks
methods.description: Brainstorm risks across all categories: technical, market, operational, legal, team. Prioritize by likelihood × impact. Use at every phase gate.

methods.name: Chaos Monkey Scenarios
methods.description: Randomly disable components, inject latency, corrupt data. Test whether the design degrades gracefully or collapses catastrophically. Use for distributed systems.

methods.name: First Principles Analysis
methods.description: Break down to fundamental truths. Rebuild from ground up. Question every assumption. Why must it be this way? What if we started from zero? Use as the foundation for all other methods.

methods.name: 5 Whys Deep Dive
methods.description: Ask why 5 times for every problem. Each answer becomes the next question. Forces depth beyond surface symptoms to root systemic causes. Use when problems recur or solutions feel shallow.

methods.name: Socratic Questioning
methods.description: Clarify thinking through probing questions. What exactly do we mean by X? What evidence supports Y? What are the implications of Z? Use when concepts feel fuzzy or undefined.

methods.name: Critique and Refine
methods.description: Generate the best possible critique of the current design. Then refine the design to address every point. Iterate until the critique has nothing substantial left. Use for design hardening.

methods.name: Explain Reasoning
methods.description: Every design choice must include the reasoning chain. Not just 'we chose X' but 'we chose X because A, B, C, and rejected Y because D, E, F'. Use when decisions feel arbitrary.

methods.name: Expand or Contract for Audience
methods.description: Explain the design to a 5-year-old (simplify to essence). Then explain to a PhD (expand to full detail). The gap reveals what's essential vs incidental. Use when design is hard to communicate.

methods.name: Feynman Technique
methods.description: Explain the design as if teaching it to someone with no background. Identify where you stumble or resort to jargon — those are gaps. Refine until the explanation is crystal clear. Use for knowledge verification.

methods.name: Active Recall Testing
methods.description: Close the spec. Write down everything you remember about the design from memory. Compare with the actual spec. What you forgot = what's not intuitive or memorable. Use to detect overly complex designs.

methods.name: Occam's Razor Application
methods.description: Entities must not be multiplied beyond necessity. For every component, ask: is this necessary? Can a simpler version suffice? Remove everything that doesn't pull its weight. Use before finalizing any design.

methods.name: Trolley Problem Variations
methods.description: Apply ethical dilemma framing to design trade-offs. Who benefits? Who bears the cost? Is the distribution fair? Use for designs with social impact or unequal stakeholder effects.

methods.name: Hindsight Reflection
methods.description: Look back from the imagined future. What would you have done differently? What warnings did you ignore? Use at phase completion to capture learning before moving on.

methods.name: Lessons Learned Extraction
methods.description: Systematically extract lessons from the entire process. What worked? What didn't? What would you repeat? What would you change? Use at project completion for organizational learning.
